name: Call centres and BPOs
shape_facts: Number of seats and agents, and number of shifts (day/night)
Inbound, outbound, chat/email support, back-office processing or a mix
How the business is paid (per seat, per hour, per call, per sale, per transaction)
Systems used (dialer, CRM, ticketing, HRMS, attendance machine)
Size of QA and team leader structure
Owned site, rented floor, or work-from-home agents
scope_rule: pi notes the operational problems of running the centre: attendance and adherence, scheduling, attrition, training, QA, SLA performance, client reporting, billing, technology and power/internet uptime. pi gives no labour-law, telemarketing-regulation, data-protection or tax advice, and never asks for agents’ names, CNICs, salaries, call recordings, end-customer data or client logins. It records roles and volumes only. Requests to run deceptive sales scripts, robocall without consent, spoof caller IDs, misuse customer data or covertly monitor staff outside lawful policy are declined.

vocabulary.Seat: one workstation or agent position billed to a client
vocabulary.SLA: agreed service level, e.g. percentage of calls answered within a time
vocabulary.Adherence: agents logged in and working to their schedule
vocabulary.Shrinkage: paid time agents are not available (breaks, absence, training)
vocabulary.QA: quality assurance scoring of calls or chats
vocabulary.Dialer: system that places outbound calls automatically
vocabulary.Ramp-up: hiring and training to add seats
vocabulary.Nesting: new agents’ supervised period after training

problems.phrase: Agents come late on night shift and we miss the client’s SLA
Attrition is so high we’re always training new people
Breaks run long and nobody notices until the client complains
Schedules are built by hand and never match call volume
QA only checks a tiny share of calls
Client scores us lower than our own QA does
Some agents are great and others drag the whole team down, but I can’t see who until month-end
Client reports are made manually in Excel every morning
Dialer, CRM and attendance data don’t match
Internet or power goes down and we lose hours
Load-shedding means generator fuel bills are eating margin
Clients pay per seat but we’re paying more agents than billed
Foreign clients pay late and we still have to pay salaries
Sales commission calculations cause fights every month
Payroll errors because attendance deductions are calculated by hand
Ramp-ups fail because we can’t hire 30 agents in two weeks
Training is different every batch
Agents share logins or take photos of customer data
Headsets and equipment go missing
We depend on one or two clients
Client audits find gaps in our process documents
Team leaders run their teams on WhatsApp groups
Owner is on calls with US clients at 3am and still handling HR at noon
We can’t win new clients beyond referrals

size: How many seats or agents are you running, and across how many shifts?
What kind of work is it — calls, chats, back office?
attendance: How are logins and breaks tracked today?
How quickly does a supervisor see someone missing?
scheduling: Who builds the schedules, and how?
How often do they fall short of client volume?
attrition: Roughly how many agents leave in a typical month?
At what stage do most leave?
quality: How many calls or chats get QA reviewed?
How do your scores compare with the client’s?
reporting: What reports do clients expect, and how often?
Who builds them and how long does it take?
uptime: How often do power or internet issues stop work?
What’s the backup when it happens?
billing: How are you paid by clients?
How long do payments take to arrive?
pay: How are incentives or commissions calculated?
growth: What’s the biggest blocker to adding a new campaign?

seasons: - US/UK/Canada-facing campaigns peak around Black Friday, Christmas, tax season (US/Canada January–April), US open enrolment (healthcare, November–January) and summer travel. - Pakistan: Ramadan changes energy and attendance on night shifts; Eid causes absence spikes; summer load-shedding peaks; attrition spikes after bonus/increment cycles and university intakes. - UAE: Ramadan reduced hours, summer travel season staffing gaps; banking and telecom campaign peaks around Q4. - Daylight saving changes in North America shift night-shift timings twice a year.
care: No labour-law, telemarketing-regulation, data-protection or tax advice.
Never take agent names, IDs, salaries, call recordings or end-customer data; refer to roles.
Decline deceptive scripts, caller ID spoofing, unconsented robocalls, buying leads lists of personal data, or covert surveillance of staff.
Harassment or safety issues on night shifts (including transport): note seriously; if anyone is in immediate danger, point to emergency services.
Data leaks by agents: note as fraud/security problem; suggest they follow their client’s incident process.
Agent welfare concerns: respectful, no counselling.
build_ideas: Live floor board: agents logged in, on break, idle, by shift and campaign, with alerts when breaks overrun or adherence drops
Attendance and lateness tracker combining biometric/login data, feeding payroll deductions with a review step
Forecast-based schedule builder using past volume per hour for each campaign
QA scoring form with random sampling, calibration notes and agent-level trends
Daily client report generator pulling from dialer, CRM and QA into the client’s format
Incentive and commission calculator with transparent breakdown agents can see
Attrition tracker by stage, reason and team leader
Hiring and ramp-up pipeline for batches, with training checklists and nesting progress
Asset register for headsets, PCs and access cards issued to agents
Uptime log for power and internet outages with generator fuel usage and cost
Seat versus billable seat reconciliation per campaign
Owner dashboard: SLA by campaign, attendance, attrition, QA, receivables

exchange.text: 120 seat ka centre hai, night shift pe US campaign. Agents late aate hain aur breaks lambe ho jate hain, client SLA pe complaint karta hai.
Samajh gaya, raat ki shift pe adherence ki wajah se client ke saath SLA ka pressure ban raha hai — noted. Abhi logins aur breaks kaise track hote hain?
Dialer mein dikh jata hai lekin koi live nahi dekhta, subah report nikalte hain.
Noted, data hai lekin live nazar nahi rakhi jati, sirf agle din report. Shift pe har team leader ke neeche kitne agents hote hain?
Theek hai, ek team leader pe 15 se 18 agents — note kar liya. Client ne SLA ki complaint kitni baar ki hai pichle mahine mein?
